item.content:encoded: Presentation is slick but the parts don’t add up to a cohesive whole. The forum stuff linked on the footnotes was interesting but took me out of the article which is bad for a piece trying as hard as this one is to be immersive. item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
If you’re attached to the text formatting, there could also be less text in that section overall. Making my way through it just felt like I was being forced to endure something unpleasant to get to the rest of the story. People who enjoy deciphering things more may feel differently.

Also, I don’t entirely remember the last version’s structure, and this does stand on its own as a piece, but it still gave me the impression that there was supposed to be much more to come on top of it later. That may be a reflection of the fact that I know you planned addition content in this setting. Either way, something can still stand on its own while introducing so many new things to be explore that it feels more introductory than anything else, and I think this falls into that category.

item.content:encoded:
I hate to sound like I'm beating a dead horse since I've posted largely the same thing on other postings of this article, but since you asked: I think the article takes too long to get off the ground, the extremely truncated transcripts are kind of tiresome to deal with, and the ultimate conclusion of the article doesn't hit me emotionally or otherwise. It feels like too much extraneous setup, which I imagine relates to your broader planned cannon, but is not an enjoyable reading experience.

There's not much you can do about my personal preferences obviously, but I would still strongly recommend reconsidering the volume of garbled logs at the start if nothing else.

item.title: Re: Maybe I'm just confused
item.content:encoded:
spoilers
confused is the way to be
  • FTL travel has its fair share of issues. The exotic matter emits a quantized field and FTL travel doesn't change that, it's the other way around. The solar sails provide means of charging and for local travel that doesn't need the unnecessary power
  • what do you mean by "aren't additive"? FTL drives don't really exist afaik, and in the realm of fantasy, having additional means to control the ship more accurately is not unheard of
  • It was meant to crash only if the wormhole reappears
  • The cryo-chamber contains who the New Earth Foundation considers The Founder, but not really the true Founder as they are off-world. They also have different views on anomalies
  • The notes at the end indicate everything was orchestrated by the Foundation, but this Foundation has transcended.
  • The O2 thing relates to the great oxygenation event of our planet which happened 2ish billion years ago.
  • The Foundation studied and used anomalies instead of fearing them and containing them from the world. There is no masquerade on Earth Prime. This is explained in more detail in Richard Larenz Personal Log and A Place to Call Your Home

Any other questions?

item.title: Maybe I'm just confused
item.content:encoded:
There's a lot of this article that doesn't make sense to me.

the Altruist-9 was constructed with a faster-than-light (FTL) drive and high efficiency solar sails.

Why bother with solar sails if you also have FTL? Solar sails have a top speed that's under .1% of lightspeed. Most FLT systems aren't additive with non-FTL tech, either. Is it supposed to 'jump' through to the target, then float around the star system? It sounds like it crashes and was always meant to crash.

Who is in the cryo camber? Who contacted the foundation through the wormhole? Was O2-less Earth home to a foundation that studied anomalies in the wild, without containment? But they didn't let the man who hated anomalies out.

item.title: Reeeepost
item.content:encoded:
Sorry everyone but it deserves a fresh shot at life, no 001 should be under +100

This rewrite should allow it to stand on its own, regardless of the tale situation. But I just need to tweak some things on those and we'll be golden too :)

There should be enough hints and implications to figure out what's happening on a larger scale.

spoiler
Netzach means Eternity
  • There are multiple real-life events and mythologies this corresponds to - GRB 060614, Great Oxygenation (timeline is a little fudged but who was around then to confirm it anyways), Sumerian mythos, etc
  • The cryo-chamber contains who the New Earth Foundation would call The Founder, but they aren't the Founder. The true founder had something else in mind when they started the Foundation
  • The notes at the end indicate everything was orchestrated by the Foundation, but this part of the Foundation has transcended to the point where their intentions are no longer discernable. The Foundation is a pluripotent god-organization.
  • The Foundation studied and used anomalies instead of fearing them and containing them from the world. There is no masquerade on Earth Prime. This is explained in more detail in Richard Larenz Personal Log and A Place to Call Your Home
  • Netzach is the 7th sefirot (the same that brings yesod, keter, etc)- 7th sefirot - 7 gods of Sumerian mythos - Literally means "eternity" - 50 immortal children - etc etc

Earth Pic compliant under public domain

probey boi compliant under CC-BY, thanks Jamie C.

I'll come up with a compliant pic for the 3rd one, mark my words
